lem-fixed-field-of-automorphisms-of-c-ov:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. The subfield of $\mathbb C$ fixed by every field automorphism $\sigma:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$ with $\sigma(q)=q$ for all $q\in\mathbb Q$ is exactly $\mathbb Q$.
lem-two-commuting-complex-2x2-matrices-a:
## Statement

Let $A,B\in M_2(\mathbb C)$ commute. There is a one-dimensional subspace of $\mathbb C^2$ invariant under both $A$ and $B$. Equivalently, in a basis beginning with a nonzero vector in that subspace, both matrices are upper triangular.
lem-sl2-matrix-invariants-by-epsilon-con:
## Statement

Assume full AC. For any finite $r\ge0$, every polynomial in the entries of $r$ complex $2\times2$ matrices invariant under simultaneous conjugation by $SL_2(\mathbb C)$ is a polynomial in traces of words in those matrices. For each given invariant only finitely many words are needed. If $Z\subseteq M_2(\mathbb C)^r$ is any closed reduced invariant algebraic subset, every invariant regular function on $Z$ is likewise a polynomial in the restricted word traces. In particular this applies to the representation variety of any finitely presented group in $SL_2(\mathbb C)$, with its determinant and relator equations. The assertion does not identify a nonsemisimple representation from its character or assert a generic representation over the character function field.
lem-equal-irreducible-sl2-traces-determi:
## Statement

Let $G$ be any group and $\rho,\rho':G\to SL_2(\mathbb C)$ be representations with $$\operatorname{tr}\rho(g)=\operatorname{tr}\rho'(g)\qquad(g\in G).$$ If $\rho$ is irreducible, then $\rho'$ is irreducible and there is $P\in SL_2(\mathbb C)$ such that $\rho'(g)=P\rho(g)P^{-1}$ for every $g$. If $\rho$ is reducible, it has the same trace character as its diagonal semisimplification $g\mapsto\operatorname{diag}(\chi(g),\chi(g)^{-1})$, where $\chi:G\to\mathbb C^*$ is the character on a common invariant line. The two diagonal characters $\chi,\chi^{-1}$ determine the same semisimple conjugacy class. This is a pointwise statement; it does not assert that an irreducible character component admits a tautological representation over its function field or prove rational quotient descent.
lem-torus-presentation-irreducible-perip:
## Statement

Let $a>b\ge2$ be coprime integers, choose integers $\alpha,\beta$ with $a\alpha+b\beta=1$, and put $G=\langle x,y\mid x^a=y^b\rangle$, $h=x^a=y^b$, $\mu=y^\alpha x^\beta$ and $\lambda=h\mu^{-ab}$. Consider all irreducible representations $\rho:G\to SL_2(\mathbb C)$, where irreducible means having no common invariant complex line. The common peripheral eigenvalue pairs $(M,L)\in(\mathbb C^*)^2$ have reduced Zariski closure with vanishing ideal $$(1+M^{2a}L)\quad\hbox{if }b=2,\qquad (M^{2ab}L^2-1)\quad\hbox{if }b>2.$$ More precisely, $\rho(h)=\epsilon I$ with $\epsilon=-1$ when $b=2$ and $\epsilon\in\{1,-1\}$ when $b>2$; each permitted sign occurs in a family realizing every point of the graph $L=\epsilon M^{-ab}$ except possibly finitely many meridian values. The displayed ideal is the ideal of the entire irreducible eigenvalue locus, not just of the exhibited families. No choice axiom is assumed.
lem-two-generator-sl2-word-traces-reduce:
## Statement

Let $A,B\in SL_2(\mathbb C)$ and put $a=\operatorname{tr}A$, $b=\operatorname{tr}B$, $c=\operatorname{tr}(AB)$. Every word matrix in $A^{\pm1},B^{\pm1}$ is a linear combination of $I,A,B,AB$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Z[a,b,c]$, computed by finite word induction. Consequently its trace is a polynomial in those three traces. If $a=b=x$ and $c=y$, the coefficients specialize to $\mathbb Z[x,y]$. The assertion includes scalar, unipotent, reducible and irreducible pairs and uses no choice axiom.
lem-absolutely-irreducible-sl2-represent:
## Statement

Let $F$ be a field of characteristic zero and let $\rho:\Gamma\to SL_2(F)$ be a representation of a finitely generated group which is absolutely irreducible, meaning that no line is invariant under all its matrices after extension to any field containing $F$. Let $K\subseteq F$ be the subfield generated by the prime field and all traces $\operatorname{tr}\rho(g)$, $g\in\Gamma$. There are words $A=\rho(a)$ and $B=\rho(b)$ and an element $\xi$ satisfying $\xi^2-(\operatorname{tr}A)\xi+1=0$, with $\xi\ne\xi^{-1}$, such that over $F(\xi)$ the representation is conjugate by a matrix in $GL_2(F(\xi))$ to one whose generator matrices all lie in $SL_2(K(\xi))$. Thus the required model field has degree at most two over $K$. The entries are obtained by explicit finite formulas from $\xi$ and the traces of $A,B,AB,C,AC,BC,ABC$ for each generator matrix $C$. If $K(\xi)\ne K$, its nonidentity automorphism is realized on this model by simultaneous conjugation with one explicit matrix in $GL_2(K(\xi))$. In particular, suppose a projective point $z\in\mathbb P^r(K(\xi))$ is obtained from the model by a construction commuting with field automorphisms and invariant under simultaneous $GL_2$ conjugation. Then $z$ is defined over $K$. This last clause requires the stated compatibility and invariance; it asserts no analytic, homology-rank or quotient-existence theorem.
lem-finite-homology-kernel-lines-have-ra:
## Statement

Let $A$ be a commutative integral domain with fraction field $F$. Let $B:A^s\to A^n$, $C:A^n\to A^t$ and $U=(u,v):A^2\to A^n$ be finite matrices with $CB=CU=0$. Put $\beta=\operatorname{rank}_F B$, $\gamma=\operatorname{rank}_F C$, and assume $$\operatorname{rank}_F(B\mid U)=\beta+1.$$ Then $h=n-\gamma-\beta\ge1$. There exists $0\ne f\in A$ such that, over $A_f$, the kernel, image and homology $H_f=\ker C_f/\operatorname{im}B_f$ have explicit free bases, with ranks $n-\gamma$, $\beta$ and $h$. The kernel $$L_f=\ker\{A_f^2\xrightarrow{U_f}H_f\}$$ is a free rank-one direct summand of $A_f^2$. In explicit homology coordinates the images of $u,v$ can be written $a e_1,b e_1$, with at least one of $a,b$ a unit of $A_f$. Hence $$L_f=A_f(-b,a).$$ All these assertions, including the displayed kernel, commute with any homomorphism $A_f\to E$ to a field. In particular they describe the actual homology kernel of the specialized matrices, not just a kernel before specialization.

If $A=\mathbb C[X]$ for a nonempty irreducible affine algebraic set $X$, this gives a regular projective kernel line $[-b:a]$ on a nonempty dense principal open subset and hence a rational map $X\dashrightarrow\mathbb P^1$. Its slope convention $-\text{second coordinate}/\text{first coordinate}$ is the projective value $[a:b]$, including zero and infinity. The rank-chart expressions agree wherever both are defined. The kernel line is unchanged by invertible changes of the three chain bases, by adding boundary columns to $U$, and by multiplying both columns of $U$ by the same invertible scalar. For rational changes it is unchanged after restricting to a common open set where their denominators and inverses are defined. No assertion that the matrix rank hypotheses hold for an arbitrary topological or representation-theoretic family is part of this lemma.
lem-nonparabolic-adjoint-torus-homology-:
## Statement

Let $F$ be a field of characteristic different from $2$, and let $L,M\in SL_2(F)$ commute. Write $t=\operatorname{tr}M$ and suppose $\Delta=t^2-4\ne0$. Give the torus $T^2$ an ordered pair of based oriented generating loops $(\lambda,\mu)$, and give its adjoint local system intrinsic monodromies $P=\operatorname{Ad}L$ and $Q=\operatorname{Ad}M$ on $V=\mathfrak{sl}_2(F)$. Here monodromy acts on column coefficient vectors on the left. Set
$$v=M-\frac t2 I,\qquad W=\{X\in V:\operatorname{tr}(vX)=0\}.$$
Then $V=Fv\oplus W$, both summands are preserved by $P,Q$, and $P,Q$ are the identity on $Fv$. There is an explicit split chain model
$$0\longrightarrow V\xrightarrow{d_2}V\oplus V\xrightarrow{d_1}V\longrightarrow0,$$
where $d_2z=((I-Q)z,(P-I)z)$ and $d_1(x,y)=(P-I)x+(Q-I)y$, in the ordered edge coordinates $(\lambda,\mu)$. Its $W$ subcomplex is contractible, so
$$H_0(T^2;V)=F[v],\qquad H_1(T^2;V)=F[v\otimes\lambda]\oplus F[v\otimes\mu],\qquad H_2(T^2;V)=F[v\otimes[T^2]].$$
In particular the two displayed peripheral classes are an actual basis, without imposing any norm-one normalization on $v$. The splitting, contraction and classes commute with field extensions and simultaneous conjugation of $L,M$. All their matrix entries are rational expressions in the entries of $L,M$, with denominators powers of $2$ and $\Delta$. This assertion concerns boundary-torus homology only: it makes no claim about the rank of its inclusion into the homology of a knot exterior.
lem-partial-projective-resolutions-deter:
## Statement

Let $R$ be any unital ring, let $S$ be a left $R$-module, and let
$$C_2\xrightarrow{d_2}C_1\xrightarrow{d_1}C_0\xrightarrow{\epsilon_C}S\longrightarrow0,\qquad D_2\xrightarrow{\delta_2}D_1\xrightarrow{\delta_1}D_0\xrightarrow{\epsilon_D}S\longrightarrow0$$
be augmented complexes of left $R$-modules, exact at $C_1,C_0,S$ and at $D_1,D_0,S$. Suppose each of the six modules $C_i,D_i$, $0\le i\le2$, is projective. No exactness at $C_2,D_2$ or further degrees is required. There are augmentation-preserving chain maps through degree $2$ between these complexes lifting $1_S$. For every right $R$-module $N$, any such comparison induces the same isomorphism of abelian groups
$$H_1(N\otimes_R C_\bullet)\ \cong\ H_1(N\otimes_R D_\bullet).$$
These isomorphisms are inverse under reversing the complexes, compose for a third such complex, and are natural in homomorphisms of right coefficient modules. In particular a supplied augmentation-preserving chain map through degree $2$ induces this isomorphism; its construction need not be the one chosen in the proof. Tensoring is not assumed exact, and $N$ need not be flat. This is a comparison of supplied algebraic complexes, not an assertion that a presentation complex is a deformation retract or a homotopy-equivalent spine of another space.
lem-laurent-algebraic-curve-has-principa:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $C$ be a finite union of distinct irreducible one-dimensional closed algebraic subsets of $(\mathbb C^*)^2$. Suppose its radical vanishing ideal in $\mathbb C[M^{\pm1},L^{\pm1}]$ is the scalar extension of a radical ideal in $\mathbb Q[M^{\pm1},L^{\pm1}]$; this is what it means here for the reduced union to be defined over $\mathbb Q$. Then its complex vanishing ideal is generated by a square-free Laurent polynomial $F$ with primitive integer coefficients. Any two such primitive integer-coefficient generators differ by multiplication by $\pm M^aL^b$, where $a,b\in\mathbb Z$.
lem-automorphism-stable-laurent-ideals-d:
## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $n\ge0$, let $R_{\mathbb Q}=\mathbb Q[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_n^{\pm1}]$ and $R_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_n^{\pm1}]$, and let $I\subseteq R_{\mathbb C}$ be an ideal invariant under coefficientwise application of every field automorphism of $\mathbb C$ fixing $\mathbb Q$. Then $$I=(I\cap R_{\mathbb Q})R_{\mathbb C}.$$ If $I$ is radical, then $I\cap R_{\mathbb Q}$ is radical as well. In particular, if $S\subseteq(\mathbb C^*)^n$ is preserved by all such coordinatewise automorphisms, the radical vanishing ideal of its Zariski closure is the scalar extension of a radical ideal over $\mathbb Q$. This includes the empty set, the whole torus and zero variables. No algebraicity or closedness of $S$ is assumed.
lem-finite-affine-incidence-projection-a:
## Statement

Assume full AC. Put $T=(\mathbb C^*)^n$ and $R=\mathbb C[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_n^{\pm1}]$, with $n\ge0$. For a finite index set $B$, let $J_b$ be an ideal of $R[u_1,\ldots,u_{m_b}]$, where $m_b\ge0$, and let $X_b$ be its zero set in $T\times\mathbb C^{m_b}$. Let $S$ be the union of the coordinate projections of the $X_b$ to $T$. Then its Zariski closure $Z$ has radical vanishing ideal $$I(Z)=\bigcap_{b\in B}\bigl(\sqrt{J_b}\cap R\bigr).$$ Write the finite irreducible-component decomposition as $Z=\bigcup_i Z_i$, and let $C$ be the union of those $Z_i$ whose dimension is one. Then $$I(C)=\bigcap_{\dim Z_i=1}I(Z_i).$$ Thus one must select the one-dimensional components after radical elimination; the first intersection alone also retains any isolated or higher-dimensional components. Empty intersections are the unit ideal and an empty selected union is empty. If $S$ is preserved by every coordinatewise field automorphism of $\mathbb C$ fixing $\mathbb Q$ (in particular, if all $J_b$ are generated by rational-coefficient Laurent polynomials), both $I(Z)$ and $I(C)$ are scalar extensions of radical ideals over $\mathbb Q$. No closedness of the projections or bound on their dimension is assumed.
def-boundary-slope-of-an-incompressible-:
## Definition

Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with chosen compact exterior $E_K$ and boundary torus $T_K=\partial E_K$. A simple closed curve on a surface is **essential** if it is not null-homotopic there. A surface $S\subset E_K$ is properly embedded if $S\cap\partial E_K=\partial S$ and its interior lies in the interior of $E_K$. It is **incompressible** if it has no embedded disk with interior disjoint from $S$ and essential boundary in $S$; it is **boundary-incompressible** if it has no embedded disk whose boundary is the union of an arc in $S$ that does not cut off a disk and an arc in $\partial E_K$. A **boundary slope** of $K$ is the unoriented isotopy class of an essential simple closed curve on $T_K$ that occurs as the boundary of a properly embedded, orientable, incompressible, boundary-incompressible surface. Using the positive meridian $\mu$ and preferred longitude $\lambda$ as a homology basis, a primitive class $a[\lambda]+b[\mu]$ has slope $b/a\in\mathbb Q\cup\{\infty\}$, with $a=0$ interpreted as $\infty$. A boundary slope is **strict** if it has a realizing orientable, incompressible, boundary-incompressible surface which is not a fiber of any locally trivial fibration $E_K\to S^1$; a fiber is the inverse image of a point under that bundle projection.
lem-presentation-complex-computes-twiste:
## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $(Y,y)$ be a path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected based space, and fix an isomorphism
$$\langle x_1,\ldots,x_n\mid r_1,\ldots,r_m\rangle\ \cong\ \Gamma=\pi_1(Y,y)$$
from a finite presentation. Let $P$ be its presentation $2$-complex, with its one vertex $p$. Choose based loops in $Y$ representing the specified generators. They extend, after choosing fillings of the finitely many relators, to a based map $f:P\to Y$ inducing the specified isomorphism. No CW structure on $Y$ is required. For every left $\mathbb Z[\Gamma]$-module $A$, interpreted as the base fibre of a local system with $g a=T_{\bar g}a$ in the first-loop-first convention, this map induces an isomorphism
$$H_1(P;f^*\mathcal A)\ \xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\ H_1(Y;\mathcal A).$$
This assertion does not require $Y$ or its universal cover to be aspherical and does not assert that $P$ is a spine or a homotopy-equivalent model of $Y$.

There is the following explicit finite-chain form. Give universal-cover chains the right action $c\cdot g=T_{g^{-1}}c$, and choose the lifted presentation vertex $e_0$ and generator edges $e_j$ starting there. For a word $w$ in the generators and their inverses, let each positive letter $x_j$ after prefix $q$ contribute $e_j\cdot q^{-1}$, and each negative letter $x_j^{-1}$ after prefix $q$ contribute $-e_j\cdot(qx_j^{-1})^{-1}$. Denote the sum by $c_w$. Then
$$\partial c_w=e_0\cdot w^{-1}-e_0.$$
If $u\in A$ is fixed by $w$, the tensor $c_w\otimes u$ is a cycle. Under the displayed isomorphism its class is the class of the actual based loop in $Y$ represented by $w$, with initial coefficient $u$; it is independent of the word representative and the relator fillings of $f$.

In particular let $j:(T^2,*)\to(Y,y)$ be a based torus map with ordered based loops $(\lambda,\mu)$, choose words $w_\lambda,w_\mu$ for their images, and let $u$ be fixed by both. The two finite cycles $c_{w_\lambda}\otimes u,c_{w_\mu}\otimes u$ compute the images of the actual torus classes in precisely this order. If $A$ is a finite-dimensional vector space over a field $F$, the presentation complex gives finite matrices $B:C_2\to C_1$, $C:C_1\to C_0$ and these two cycle columns $U$, with $CB=CU=0$. The actual kernel of the two peripheral classes mapping into $H_1(Y;\mathcal A)$ is exactly
$$\ker\{F^2\xrightarrow{U}\ker C/\operatorname{im}B\}.$$
Thus a one-dimensional image of those two actual peripheral classes is equivalent to $\operatorname{rank}_F(B\mid U)=\operatorname{rank}_FB+1$. All matrix entries are finite sums of matrices for generator words and their inverses. For the left coefficient action $\operatorname{Ad}\rho$ of an $SL_2$ representation they are polynomial in the representation entries and in the chosen vector $u$. For a torus restriction with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\mu))^2\ne4$, one may take $u=\rho(\mu)-\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\mu))I$ in characteristic different from $2$; the two torus classes are then a basis. This applies, in particular, to an actual compact smooth knot exterior and its based peripheral torus map. No existence of a generic representation family or generic exterior rank is inferred.
def-sl-two-abelian-surgery:
## Definition

Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $p,q\in\mathbb Z$ be coprime and not both zero, and let $E_K(p/q)$ be the Dehn filling whose attached solid-torus meridian is identified with $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$. A closed 3-manifold $Y$ is **$SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian** if every homomorphism $\pi_1(Y)\to SL_2(\mathbb C)$ has abelian image. The slope $p/q$ is an **$SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian surgery slope** for $K$ if $E_K(p/q)$ is $SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian. The knot admits infinitely many such surgeries if infinitely many distinct rational slopes have this property.
def-sl-two-character-variety-and-periphe:
## Definition

Assume full AC. Let $G=\pi_1(E_K)$ be the group of a smooth oriented knot exterior, with positive meridian $\mu$ and preferred longitude $\lambda$. For a finite presentation $G=\langle g_1,\ldots,g_n\mid r_1,\ldots,r_m\rangle$, the **$SL_2(\mathbb C)$ representation variety** is the algebraic set of tuples $(A_1,\ldots,A_n)\in SL_2(\mathbb C)^n$ for which every relator matrix $r_j(A_1,\ldots,A_n)$ equals the identity. The group $SL_2(\mathbb C)$ acts on this set by simultaneous conjugation. Its affine categorical quotient, whose coordinate ring is the invariant ring of regular functions, is the **$SL_2(\mathbb C)$ character variety** $X(E_K)$. For a representation $\rho$, its character is the function $\gamma\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\gamma))$. A representation is **reducible** if its matrices preserve a common one-dimensional subspace of $\mathbb C^2$; otherwise it is irreducible. The peripheral torus group is $\pi_1(T_K)\cong\mathbb Z^2$, generated by the meridian and preferred longitude; its image in $G$ is generated by their commuting classes and need not be isomorphic to $\mathbb Z^2$. Their image under any representation is a commuting pair of matrices, so it has a common invariant line and is simultaneously triangularizable over $\mathbb C$. Choosing a common invariant line gives meridian and longitude eigenvalues $(M,L)\in(\mathbb C^*)^2$; the unordered boundary character identifies $(M,L)$ with $(M^{-1},L^{-1})$. Simultaneous diagonalizability is stronger than simultaneous triangularizability.
lem-nonseparating-longitudinal-surface-i:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a fibered knot with exterior $E_K$ and fiber surface $F$. If $S\subset E_K$ is a connected, orientable, nonseparating, incompressible properly embedded surface whose boundary is a nonempty union of longitudes, then $S$ is isotopic to $F$. After their boundary curves are identified by an isotopy in the boundary torus and this alignment is extended across a collar, the concluding isotopy may be taken relative to the aligned boundary.
lem-sl2-representation-variety-is-affine:
## Statement

Assume full AC and let $G=\pi_1(E_K)=\langle g_1,\ldots,g_n\mid r_1,\ldots,r_m\rangle$ be a finite presentation of a knot-exterior group. The set of homomorphisms $G\to SL_2(\mathbb C)$ is the affine algebraic subset of $SL_2(\mathbb C)^n$ cut out by the matrix-entry equations $r_j(A_1,\ldots,A_n)=I_2$ for $1\le j\le m$. After each inverse letter is replaced by the adjugate of its determinant-one matrix, these equations have integer coefficients in the matrix-entry coordinates.
lem-figure-eight-two-meridian-presentati:
## Statement

Assume full AC and use the standard oriented four-crossing figure-eight code of the explicit oriented Wirtinger-code lemma, with its positive based under-arc meridians $x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4$ and compatible diagram access paths. Put $u=x_1$, $v=x_2$, and $w=uv^{-1}u^{-1}v$. Then $$\pi_1(E_{4_1})=\langle u,v\mid vw=wu\rangle,$$ with $u$ a positive meridian. In this presentation $$X_3=uvu^{-1},\qquad X_4=v^{-1}uvu^{-1}v=w^{-1}v$$ are the old $x_3,x_4$. The preferred longitude based compatibly with $u$ is represented by $$\lambda=X_4u^{-1}vX_3^{-1}.$$ In particular its trace in any representation is the trace of this explicit word. The formula does not identify a zero-homology centralizing word as a longitude without the diagram-parallel calculation.
def-adjoint-twisted-homology-and-culler-:
## Definition

Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, $E_K$ its exterior, and $ho:\pi_1(E_K)	o SL_2(\mathbb C)$ a representation. The **adjoint local system** $\operatorname{Ad}ho$ has fibre $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$ and left group-module action $\gamma\cdot v=ho(\gamma)vho(\gamma)^{-1}$. In the first-loop-first intrinsic convention, this means forward path transport $T_\gamma(v)=ho(\gamma)^{-1}vho(\gamma)$; equivalently the corresponding right action is $v\cdot\gamma=ho(\gamma)^{-1}vho(\gamma)$. Its twisted homology $H_*(E_K;\operatorname{Ad}ho)$ is the intrinsic local-system homology with these transports, equivalently the homology of the cellular local-coefficient complex for a supplied CW structure; the same convention defines boundary-torus twisted homology and the inclusion map $i_*:H_1(\partial E_K;\operatorname{Ad}ho)	o H_1(E_K;\operatorname{Ad}ho)$. An **admissible adjoint representation** is one for which there is a nonzero vector $v_ho\in\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$ fixed by the peripheral adjoint action such that $\{[v_ho\otimes\lambda],[v_ho\otimes\mu]\}$ is a basis of $H_1(\partial E_K;\operatorname{Ad}ho)$ and $\ker i_*$ is one-dimensional. For an irreducible affine character curve $X$, its function field $\mathbb C(X)$ is the fraction field of its coordinate domain. A **tautological representation** over $\mathbb C(X)$ is a homomorphism $ho_X:\pi_1(E_K)	o SL_2(\mathbb C(X))$ whose character is the generic character of $X$. A **smooth projective completion** consists of a smooth complete curve $\overline X$ with a dense open subset $U$ identified with the normalization $X^
u$ of $X$, with its finite birational normalization map $
u:U	o X$ recorded. When $X$ is smooth, $
u$ identifies $U$ with $X$, recovering the usual completion. An **ideal point** is a point $x\in\overline X\setminus U$; points of $U$ over singular affine points of $X$ are affine branches and are retained inside $U$. Such an ideal point defines the discrete valuation $v_x(f)=\operatorname{ord}_x(f)$ on $\mathbb C(X)$. The valuation ring is $\mathcal O_x=\{f:v_x(f)\ge0\}$, and a **uniformizer** is an element $\pi\in\mathcal O_x$ with $v_x(\pi)=1$. Its residue field is $k_x=\mathcal O_x/(\pi)$. An $\mathcal O_x$-lattice in $\mathbb C(X)^2$ is a free rank-two $\mathcal O_x$-submodule spanning $\mathbb C(X)^2$; two lattices are homothetic if one is a nonzero scalar multiple of the other. The **Bruhat–Tits tree** has homothety classes of these lattices as vertices, with two vertices adjacent if representatives satisfy $\pi\Lambda\subsetneq\Lambda'\subsetneq\Lambda$ and $\Lambda/\Lambda'$ is one-dimensional over $k_x$. Whenever the tautological representation exists, it acts on this tree. The ideal point, valuation, action, and any essential surface produced from the action are its Culler–Shalen data; that surface is called the associated Culler–Shalen surface.
lem-knot-boundary-eigenvalue-locus-defin:
## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with a finite Wirtinger presentation by words in generators and their inverses, and let $\mu,\lambda$ be its marked meridian and preferred-longitude words. Let $\mathcal E_K\subset(\mathbb C^*)^2$ consist of the pairs $(M,L)$ for which some representation $\rho:\pi_1(E_K)\to SL_2(\mathbb C)$ has a common eigenline for $\rho(\mu)$ and $\rho(\lambda)$ with eigenvalues $M$ and $L$. Then the Zariski closure of $\mathcal E_K$ is defined over $\mathbb Q$: its radical vanishing ideal in $\mathbb C[M^{\pm1},L^{\pm1}]$ is obtained by extending scalars from a radical ideal in $\mathbb Q[M^{\pm1},L^{\pm1}]$.
lem-sl2-trace-functions-are-regular-and-:
## Statement

Assume full AC. For every word $w$ in the generators of a finitely presented group $G$, the function $\rho\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(\rho(w))$ is a regular function on $\operatorname{Hom}(G,SL_2(\mathbb C))$ and is invariant under simultaneous conjugation.
def-knot-a-polynomial:
## Definition

Assume full AC and let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with exterior $E_K$, positive meridian $\mu$, and preferred longitude $\lambda$. Define $\mathcal E_K\subset(\mathbb C^*)^2$ to consist of all pairs $(M,L)$ for which some representation $\rho:\pi_1(E_K)\to SL_2(\mathbb C)$ has a common invariant line on which $\rho(\mu)$ acts by $M$ and $\rho(\lambda)$ acts by $L$. The Zariski closure is the smallest Zariski-closed algebraic subset containing $\mathcal E_K$; let $V_K$ be the union of its one-dimensional irreducible components, where an irreducible component is a maximal irreducible closed subset. Zero-dimensional image components are omitted. The **ordinary A-polynomial** $A_K(M,L)$ is the Laurent polynomial generating the vanishing ideal of $V_K$, chosen square-free (no repeated irreducible factors) and with primitive integer coefficients (their greatest common divisor is one). It is determined up to multiplication by $\pm M^aL^b$ for $a,b\in\mathbb Z$. Its reduced curve includes the abelian component $L=1$; equivalently, its representative in $\mathbb Z[M,L]$ is divisible by $L-1$.
lem-sl2-character-trace-coordinate-algeb:
## Statement

Assume full AC and let $G$ be a finitely presented group. Every regular function on $\operatorname{Hom}(G,SL_2(\mathbb C))$ invariant under simultaneous conjugation is a polynomial in finitely many word-trace functions $t_w(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(w))$. Equivalently, the coordinate algebra of the affine character quotient is generated by trace functions of words in $G$.
def-enhanced-a-polynomial:
## Definition

Assume full AC and let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot. The **enhanced A-polynomial** $\widetilde A_K(M,L)$ is the primitive square-free Laurent polynomial defining the union of one-dimensional peripheral-eigenvalue image components arising from irreducible characters of $\pi_1(E_K)$. It is defined up to multiplication by $\pm M^aL^b$. The ordinary A-polynomial is the least common multiple $A_K=\operatorname{lcm}(\widetilde A_K,L-1)$, up to a Laurent unit, where the least common multiple uses each distinct irreducible Laurent factor only once; the factor $L-1$ is the contribution of the abelian character component, and an irreducible component may also contribute that same factor.
lem-sl-two-character-trace-coordinate-mo:
## Statement

Assume full AC and let $G=\pi_1(E_K)$ have a finite presentation. There is a finite list of words $w_1,\ldots,w_N\in G$ whose trace functions generate the coordinate ring of $X(E_K)$, so the map $[\rho]\mapsto(\operatorname{tr}\rho(w_1),\ldots,\operatorname{tr}\rho(w_N))$ is a closed embedding into $\mathbb C^N$, with defining ideal the kernel of the induced map $\mathbb C[z_1,\ldots,z_N]\to\mathbb C[\operatorname{Hom}(G,SL_2)]^{SL_2}$. On the irreducible-character locus, equal trace coordinates determine conjugate representations; on the reducible locus, the quotient records the semisimplified diagonal character, not the possibly non-diagonalizable representative.
def-character-variety-logarithmic-slope-:
## Definition

Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $\rho:\pi_1(E_K)\to SL_2(\mathbb C)$ have admissible adjoint local system, and let $v_\rho$ be a nonzero peripheral-adjoint-invariant vector for which $[v_\rho\otimes\lambda],[v_\rho\otimes\mu]$ form the specified ordered basis of $H_1(\partial E_K;\operatorname{Ad}\rho)$. If a generator of the one-dimensional kernel of inclusion is $a[v_\rho\otimes\lambda]+b[v_\rho\otimes\mu]$, the **Bénard–Florens–Rodau slope** is $s_K(\rho)=-b/a\in\mathbb C\cup\{\infty\}$, with $a=0$ interpreted as $\infty$. Rescaling $v_\rho$ or the kernel generator does not change this projective ratio. A rational function on an irreducible character component means an element of its function field, the fraction field of its coordinate domain. A projective-valued rational function means a point of the projective line over that field; it may be identically $\infty$. The slope's rational extension has this projective meaning. Unless its generic value is $\infty$, it is an ordinary rational function, whose individual infinite values are poles. Its rational extension is not a value assigned to every singular or inadmissible character.
lem-figure-eight-character-and-longitude:
## Statement

Assume full AC and let $K=J(2,-2)$ be the figure-eight knot. Use the two-bridge group presentation $\pi_1(E_K)=\langle u,v\mid v w=w u\rangle$, where $w=uv^{-1}u^{-1}v$, and take $\mu=u$. On the one-dimensional irreducible character component, define $x(\chi)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(u))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(v))$ and $y(\chi)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(uv))$. Then
$$2x^2+y^2-x^2y-y-1=0,$$
and the preferred-longitude trace is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\lambda))=x^4-5x^2+2$. The displayed curve equation is irreducible over $\mathbb C$, and $x$ is nonconstant on it.
lem-knot-a-polynomial-boundary-eliminati:
## Statement

Assume full AC and let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot. The restriction of representations of $\pi_1(E_K)$ to the peripheral torus gives an eigenvalue locus in $(\mathbb C^*)^2$ with algebraic Zariski closure. Its one-dimensional reduced image components are exactly the curve components used in $A_K(M,L)$; isolated image points contribute no curve factor. Radical elimination of the representation, trace and eigenline coordinates from the finite presentation incidence equations, followed by retaining precisely the one-dimensional irreducible components, yields the Laurent ideal of that curve union, whose square-free primitive generator is $A_K$ up to $\pm M^aL^b$.
lem-torus-knot-enhanced-a-polynomial:
## Statement

Assume full AC and let $a>b\ge2$ be coprime positive integers. With the meridian-longitude and exponent conventions used for the enhanced A-polynomial, the enhanced A-polynomial of $T_{a,b}$ is, up to multiplication by a Laurent unit,
$$\widetilde A_{T_{a,b}}(M,L)=\begin{cases}1+M^{2a}L,&b=2,\\-1+M^{2ab}L^2,&b>2.\end{cases}$$
If $K$ is the unknot, then $\widetilde A_K=1$. The nontrivial torus-knot Newton polygon is therefore a line segment whose slope in the $(a,b)\mapsto M^bL^a$ convention is $ab$.
lem-irreducible-sl2-character-components:
## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $G$ be finitely presented, let its reduced complex $SL_2$ representation variety have its trace-coordinate affine character quotient, and let $X$ be a nonempty irreducible closed subset of that quotient containing an irreducible character. Write $A=\mathbb C[X]$ and $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$. There is a field $L/K$ of degree at most two and an absolutely irreducible representation $\sigma:G\to SL_2(L)$ whose every word trace is the corresponding function on $X$.

More precisely, for some $0\ne f\in A$ there is a subring $B\subset L$ which is either $A_f$ or the free rank-two algebra $A_f[\xi]=A_f[T]/(T^2-aT+1)$, where $a$ is one word trace and $a^2-4$ is a unit. All generator matrices lie in $SL_2(B)$. Every $\chi\in D_X(f)$ admits a homomorphism $B\to\mathbb C$ extending evaluation at $\chi$; every resulting representation has character $\chi$ and is irreducible. This is an actual family of representatives, not merely agreement of formal traces. One can enlarge $f$ to make any specified finite list of nonzero elements of $L$ and their inverses belong to $B$.

If $[L:K]=2$, its nonidentity automorphism $\tau$ acts on $\sigma$ by simultaneous conjugation with an explicit matrix $P\in GL_2(L)$. Consequently any projective point obtained from $\sigma$ by finite field operations that commute with field automorphisms and whose value is invariant under simultaneous $GL_2$ conjugation is defined over $K$. This clause presumes that the construction is actually defined and invariant; it supplies no homological rank, tangent-space or essential-surface assertion.
lem-adjoint-twisted-slope-is-rational-on:
## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $X$ be an irreducible component of the $SL_2(\mathbb C)$ character variety of a knot exterior that contains irreducible characters and has a nonempty dense Zariski-open locus of scheme-smooth, non-boundary-parabolic admissible characters. On this locus the Bénard–Florens–Rodau slope is invariant under conjugation and extends to a rational map $X\dashrightarrow\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)$; when $X$ is one-dimensional its generic value lies in $\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C(X))$, and unless it is identically $\infty$ it is an ordinary rational function in $\mathbb C(X)$.
thm-a-polynomial-boundary-restriction-an:
## Statement

Assume full AC and let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with exterior $E_K$, meridian $\mu$, and preferred longitude $\lambda$. Restriction to the peripheral torus induces an algebraic map from the character variety of $E_K$ to that of the torus. Every one-dimensional peripheral eigenvalue image component is contained in the zero set of the ordinary A-polynomial, while isolated image points are not treated as curve factors. For a primitive pair $(p,q)\in\mathbb Z^2$ (with $q=0$ denoting the meridional slope), a representation $\rho:\pi_1(E_K)\to SL_2(\mathbb C)$ descends to the filling that kills $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$ exactly when $\rho(\mu)^p\rho(\lambda)^q=I_2$. If the peripheral matrices are simultaneously diagonalizable with eigenvalues $(M,L)$ on a common eigenline, this matrix condition is equivalent to $M^pL^q=1$; without that diagonalizability, the eigenvalue equation is only necessary and the matrix relation must be checked.
thm-ccgls-newton-edge-slope-is-boundary-:
## Statement

Assume full AC and let $K\subset S^3$ be a nontrivial smooth knot. Form the Newton polygon of the ordinary A-polynomial using the exponent convention that the lattice point $(a,b)$ represents the monomial $M^bL^a$, so edge slopes are measured in the preferred meridian-longitude convention. Every finite rational slope or infinite slope of an edge of this Newton polygon is a boundary slope of an incompressible, boundary-incompressible, orientable surface in the knot exterior. This statement does not assert that the realizing surface is non-fibered or that the slope is strict.
thm-adjoint-logarithmic-gauss-slope-and-:
## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $X$ be an irreducible one-dimensional character component whose peripheral eigenvalue image is a curve component $A_X(M,L)=0$ of the ordinary A-polynomial. At a smooth point where $M,L\ne0$, $\partial_M A_X\ne0$, and $\partial_L A_X\ne0$, the rational adjoint-twisted slope is
$$s_K=-\frac{M}{L}\frac{\partial_M A_X}{\partial_L A_X}.$$
If $x$ is an ideal point of the smooth projective completion of this curve and the associated Culler-Shalen construction yields an essential surface of boundary slope $r$ in the fixed meridian-longitude convention, the limiting slope at $x$ is $-r$.
thm-enhanced-a-polynomial-newton-edge-is:
## Statement

Assume full AC and let $K\subset S^3$ be a nontrivial knot. Every finite rational or infinite slope of an edge of the Newton polygon of the enhanced A-polynomial is a strict boundary slope of $K$: it is realized by an incompressible, boundary-incompressible, orientable surface in the exterior which is not a fiber of any exterior fibration over $S^1$.
thm-benard-florens-rodau-logarithmic-gau:
## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, and let $X$ be a one-dimensional irreducible component of its $SL_2(\mathbb C)$ character variety whose peripheral image is a curve in $(\mathbb C^*)^2$. With Bénard–Florens–Rodau's variable order $A_K(L,M)$ and their slope convention, on the admissible smooth locus where the displayed derivatives are nonzero,
$$s_K(\rho)=-\frac{M}{L}\frac{\partial_M A_K}{\partial_L A_K}.$$
At an ideal point of the curve, if the associated Culler-Shalen surface has boundary slope $r$ measured by $a[\lambda]+b[\mu]$ with $r=b/a$, the limiting Bénard–Florens–Rodau slope is $-r$.
lem-baldwin-sivek-instanton-surgery-and-:
## Statement

Assume full AC and let $K\subset S^3$ be a knot. The input package required by the Baldwin–Sivek thin-knot and infinitely-many-abelian-surgeries arguments consists of the following conclusions with their stated hypotheses: (i) a nontrivial $\mathrm{SU}(2)$-averse knot has a unique rational accumulation slope and either it or its mirror is an instanton L-space knot; (ii) a nontrivial instanton L-space knot is fibered and its symmetrized Alexander polynomial has coefficients in $\{-1,0,1\}$ with nonzero coefficients alternating in sign; (iii) the L-space satellite restrictions and the pattern/companion surgery-transfer statements exclude the satellite cases used in §§3–5; and (iv) the hyperbolic Dehn-filling theorem and the knot-exterior JSJ classification reduce the remaining cases to torus knots. This carrier records the exact imported result interfaces and does not assert that these conclusions have been proved locally.
thm-baldwin-sivek-infinitely-many-abelia:
## Statement

Assume full AC. A smooth knot $K\subset S^3$ admits infinitely many distinct rational $SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian Dehn surgeries if and only if $K$ is a torus knot, with the unknot included as a torus knot with one parameter of absolute value one.
thm-enhanced-a-polynomial-newton-polygon:
## Statement

Assume full AC and let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth knot. For a nonzero Laurent polynomial $f(M,L)$, its Newton polygon is the convex hull in $\mathbb R^2$ of exponent pairs $(a,b)$ for which the coefficient of $M^bL^a$ is nonzero. The enhanced A-polynomial is **thin** when this polygon is contained in an affine line; the constant polynomial $1$ has a one-point Newton polygon and is thin. Then the enhanced A-polynomial of $K$ is thin if and only if $K$ is a torus knot, including the unknot.
cor-enhanced-a-polynomial-and-alexander-:
## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $a\ge b\ge1$ be coprime positive integers, and let $T_{a,b}\subset S^3$ be the corresponding torus knot. If a knot $K\subset S^3$ has the same enhanced A-polynomial as $T_{a,b}$ up to a Laurent unit and the same Alexander-polynomial breadth (highest exponent minus lowest exponent of its symmetrized Alexander polynomial), then $K$ has the same underlying unoriented knot type as $T_{a,b}$. When $b\ge2$, the absolute torus parameters of $K$ agree with $\{a,b\}$.
thm-baldwin-sivek-two-boundary-slope-alt:
## Statement

Assume full AC. If $K\subset S^3$ is a nontrivial fibered knot that is not a torus knot, then either its exterior contains a connected, separating, incompressible surface whose boundary curves have slope zero, or $K$ has at least three distinct boundary slopes.
